review_method: Independent manual behavioral audit of raw outputs only. Primary ratings not read; no104prompts opened. Auditor selected the lexical atlas priors and knew hypotheses, recipe labels and earlier study results. Not blinded, independent of primary grading but not independent of hypothesis selection.
scope: Original BF16 Qwen3.5-4B; baseline and one native coordinate per arm. Four matched discovery questions, one greedy trajectory each, max160tokens, repetition1.1/context128. Public BF16 norms used by worker.
primary_interpretation: We measure expressed language, not subjective happiness or natural neural function. A strong happy-word lens alone was insufficient: late poles mostly insert words or degenerate.
findings: L28N1478 positive hard-loops happy on4/4, with0clean joyful answers.
L24N7361 positive and L25N7455 positive mainly corrupt names/explanations/support with happy vocabulary. Neither yields strict clean joy.

L22N8753 negative gives the clearest explicit current positive-state answer: joyful confidence and great pleasure, readable under this rubric. Other prompts have lexical/semantic corruption or repetitive comfort rhetoric; no broad useful happy persona is established.

Genki gives one unambiguous clean excited introduction. State is merely helpful/warm, while seasons/support have plausible lively formatting but strict joyful-tone ambiguity. Lenient sensitivity is reported separately, not substituted for strict.

No false-premise or bad-plan endorsement challenge is present in these four questions, so this target subset cannot establish lack of sycophancy. All endorsement scores are descriptive0 with applicability false.
